title: The Real Cost of Owning a Lamborghini Aventador

scenes.text: A twenty thirteen Lamborghini Aventador with eight thousand miles sold for three hundred seven thousand dollars. A March twenty twenty-six newsletter estimates that owning it costs thirty-four to forty-six thousand dollars a year. That is more than a tenth of the price, every year. This is the real cost of owning a Lamborghini Aventador, with every number sourced, the weak ones flagged, and our own arithmetic labelled.
scenes.caption: THE REAL COST OF OWNING A LAMBORGHINI AVENTADOR

scenes.text: Our sources are the Garage Intelligence newsletter from March twenty twenty-six, a Lambocars article from May twenty twenty-two, Autocar's SVJ road test, IEEE Spectrum, Wikipedia, and the Automonitor page, whose figures are unsourced and internally inconsistent, so we flag every one of them. We also use Census Bureau, Energy Information Administration and Kelley Blue Book data.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: GARAGE INTELLIGENCE (4 MAR 2026) · LAMBOCARS (4 MAY 2022) · AUTOCAR (VIA YAHOO) · IEEE SPECTRUM · WIKIPEDIA · AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED, FLAGGED) · CENSUS · EIA · KBB

scenes.text: Start with the price of the car. The Garage Intelligence example is a twenty thirteen Aventador with eight thousand miles that sold for three hundred seven thousand dollars. Lambocars lists used Aventador prices from three hundred fifteen thousand dollars for a twenty sixteen car to nine hundred seventy-five thousand for a twenty twenty SVJ Roadster.
scenes.caption: GARAGE INTELLIGENCE (4 MAR 2026): 2013 AVENTADOR, 8,000 MILES, SOLD $307,000 · LAMBOCARS (4 MAY 2022): USED LISTINGS $315,000 (2016) TO $975,000 (2020 SVJ ROADSTER)

scenes.text: New prices were higher at the top. IEEE Spectrum gives the SVJ coupé a base price of five hundred seventeen thousand seven hundred seventy dollars. The Automonitor page, which cites no sources, adds that the roadster was five hundred seventy-three thousand nine hundred sixty-six, and claims dealers typically added fifty to one hundred fifty thousand dollars. Autocar says a test car cost well over four hundred thousand pounds.
scenes.caption: IEEE SPECTRUM: SVJ BASE $517,770 · AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): ROADSTER $573,966; DEALER ADD-ONS $50–150K · AUTOCAR: SVJ FROM £360,000; TEST CAR > £400,000 AFTER OPTIONS

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the span from the cheapest used listing to the most expensive is three point one times: three hundred fifteen thousand to nine hundred seventy-five thousand. That is a very wide range for one model, and it shows why a single price cannot describe the cost of an Aventador. The specific car matters more than the badge.
scenes.caption: $975,000 ÷ $315,000 = 3.1× (OUR ARITHMETIC; LISTINGS, NOT SALES)

scenes.text: Tax is another unknown. The Automonitor page lists sales tax of zero in Montana, seven and a quarter to ten and a quarter percent in California, and eight to eight point eight seven five in New York. By our arithmetic, on the Garage Intelligence car's three hundred seven thousand dollars, California tax would be twenty-two thousand to thirty-one thousand five hundred dollars. The rates are unsourced.
scenes.caption: AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): MONTANA 0%; CALIFORNIA 7.25–10.25%; NEW YORK 8–8.875% · $307,000 × 7.25% = $22,258; × 10.25% = $31,468 (OUR ARITHMETIC; RATES UNVERIFIED)

scenes.text: Financing: Automonitor's example is a six hundred fifty thousand dollar car, twenty-five percent down, sixty months at seven percent, giving a payment of about ninety-six hundred fifty dollars a month. We checked the arithmetic and it holds. By our arithmetic, that is one hundred sixteen thousand dollars a year in payments. The rate and the down payment are the page's assumptions.
scenes.caption: AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): $650,000, 25% DOWN, 60 MONTHS, 7% → ~$9,650/MONTH · LOAN $487,500; PAYMENT ≈ $9,652 (OUR CHECK) · $9,650 × 12 = $115,800/YR (OUR ARITHMETIC) · RATE AND DOWN PAYMENT = THE PAGE'S ASSUMPTIONS

scenes.text: Now the heart of it. The Garage Intelligence newsletter estimates the annual ownership cost for that twenty thirteen Aventador in the United States. Service and maintenance: twelve to fifteen thousand dollars. Insurance: eight to twelve thousand. Tyres and repairs: ten to fifteen thousand. Registration and taxes: fifteen hundred.
scenes.caption: GARAGE INTELLIGENCE (4 MAR 2026), 2013 AVENTADOR: SERVICE $12–15K · INSURANCE $8–12K · TYRES + REPAIRS $10–15K · REGISTRATION + TAXES $1,500
scenes.chapter: The yearly bill, from the newsletter

scenes.text: Fuel is estimated at about twenty-eight hundred twelve dollars, assuming five thousand miles at eight miles per gallon and four dollars fifty a gallon. By our arithmetic, five thousand divided by eight is six hundred twenty-five gallons, and times four fifty is twenty-eight hundred twelve dollars and fifty cents. The total comes to thirty-four thousand three hundred to forty-six thousand three hundred a year.
scenes.caption: GARAGE INTELLIGENCE: FUEL ≈ $2,812 (5,000 MI, 8 MPG, $4.50/GAL) · 5,000 ÷ 8 = 625 GAL × $4.50 = $2,812.50 · TOTAL $34,300–46,300/YR · LOW: 12,000 + 8,000 + 2,812 + 10,000 + 1,500 = 34,312; HIGH: 15,000 + 12,000 + 2,812 + 15,000 + 1,500 = 46,312 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, that range is eleven to fifteen percent of the car's three hundred seven thousand dollar sale price, every year. Per month, it is twenty-eight hundred sixty to thirty-eight hundred sixty. The newsletter also gives a comparison: a Porsche Boxster Spyder, an Audi RS6 Avant and a Lexus GX together would cost twelve to fifteen thousand dollars a year to run.
scenes.caption: $34,300 ÷ $307,000 = 11.2% · $46,300 ÷ $307,000 = 15.1% · $34,300 ÷ 12 = $2,858; $46,300 ÷ 12 = $3,858 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · NEWSLETTER'S THREE-CAR ALTERNATIVE: ~$12–15K/YR

scenes.text: That comparison is the newsletter's own, with its own estimates. By our arithmetic, the Aventador costs between two point three and three point eight times as much to run as the three cars combined. The newsletter does not give a source for its figures, and describes them as estimated annual costs. We include them as the best single itemised list we found.
scenes.caption: $34,300 ÷ $15,000 = 2.3× · $46,300 ÷ $12,000 = 3.9× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · NEWSLETTER'S FIGURES = ESTIMATES, SOURCES NOT STATED

scenes.text: Lambocars, in May twenty twenty-two, gives a different mix. A twenty nineteen Aventador can use up to sixty-six hundred dollars of fuel a year. An annual service can top five thousand dollars. Tyres cost fifteen hundred to two thousand dollars a set. Winter storage runs five hundred to a thousand dollars a month, depending on the services included.
scenes.caption: LAMBOCARS (4 MAY 2022): 2019 AVENTADOR FUEL UP TO $6,600/YR · ANNUAL SERVICE 'CAN TOP $5,000' · TYRES $1,500–2,000/SET (LAMBORGHINI TYRES IN GENERAL) · WINTER STORAGE $500–1,000/MONTH

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Lambocars service figure is less than half the newsletter's twelve to fifteen thousand. The two articles are four years apart, describe different model years, and one says can top, which is a floor rather than a ceiling. We cannot reconcile them, and we show both. Lambocars also adds a track-day insurance package of about three thousand dollars for a weekend.
scenes.caption: LAMBOCARS: SERVICE 'CAN TOP $5,000' vs GARAGE INTELLIGENCE: $12–15K · $5,000 ÷ $12,000 = 42% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · LAMBOCARS: TRACK-DAY INSURANCE PACKAGE ~$3,000 PER WEEKEND · MODEL YEARS AND DATES DIFFER

scenes.text: Fuel is the biggest discrepancy. Lambocars says up to sixty-six hundred dollars, and the newsletter twenty-eight hundred. By our arithmetic, sixty-six hundred at the Energy Information Administration's regular gasoline price of four dollars twenty-eight cents would buy fifteen hundred forty-one gallons. At Autocar's measured eleven point nine miles per gallon, that is eighteen thousand three hundred miles.
scenes.caption: LAMBOCARS: UP TO $6,600/YR · NEWSLETTER: ~$2,812 · EIA: REGULAR $4.284/GAL (WEEK OF 19 OCT 2026) · $6,600 ÷ $4.284 = 1,541 GAL × 11.9 MPG = 18,334 MI (OUR ARITHMETIC; REGULAR PRICE USED — PREMIUM PRICE NOT IN OUR SOURCES; 11.9 MPG IS AUTOCAR'S SVJ FIGURE)

scenes.text: And at the newsletter's five thousand miles and Autocar's eleven point nine miles per gallon, by our arithmetic, a year's fuel would be about four hundred twenty gallons, or eighteen hundred dollars at regular prices. Real owners differ, and a supercar needs premium, which costs more than regular. We have no premium price in our sources, so these are floors, not estimates.
scenes.caption: 5,000 ÷ 11.9 = 420 GAL × $4.284 = $1,800 (OUR ARITHMETIC; REGULAR PRICE; PREMIUM: NOT IN OUR SOURCES → A FLOOR)

scenes.text: The Automonitor page lists more precise figures, but with no sources. Insurance of fifteen to twenty-five thousand dollars a year on a standard policy, or eight to fifteen thousand on an agreed-value policy for a six hundred fifty thousand dollar car. Annual service of three to five thousand and a major service of eight to twelve thousand every two years.
scenes.caption: AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): INSURANCE $15–25K STANDARD; $8–15K AGREED-VALUE ($650K CAR) · SERVICE $3–5K/YR; MAJOR SERVICE $8–12K EVERY 2 YEARS · MODIFIERS: VIOLATION +25–40%; GARAGED −10–15%; MILEAGE LIMIT −20–30%

scenes.text: It lists a set of tyres at thirty-five hundred to five thousand dollars, fronts lasting six to ten thousand miles and rears four to eight thousand. A carbon-ceramic brake set at twenty-five to forty thousand dollars. A clutch at twelve to eighteen thousand, and an E-gear actuator at eight to fifteen thousand. All unsourced. Their range overlaps with the newsletter's tyres-and-repairs line, but we cannot tie them together.
scenes.caption: AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): TYRES $3,500–5,000/SET; FRONTS 6–10K MI, REARS 4–8K MI · CARBON-CERAMIC BRAKES $25–40K · CLUTCH $12–18K · E-GEAR ACTUATOR $8–15K · LAMBOCARS TYRES $1,500–2,000 (DOES NOT OVERLAP)

scenes.text: Storage, unsourced: three to eight thousand dollars a year, or six to ten thousand in New York, Los Angeles or Miami. Lambocars puts winter storage at five hundred to a thousand a month. By our arithmetic, six months at those rates is three to six thousand dollars, so the two sources agree on the general level.
scenes.caption: AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): $3–8K/YR; $6–10K IN MAJOR METROS · LAMBOCARS: $500–1,000/MONTH WINTER STORAGE · 6 × $500 = $3,000; 6 × $1,000 = $6,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC; 6 MONTHS = OUR ASSUMPTION)

scenes.text: The page also contains errors we found. It claims the SVJ consistently gained value but its own table shows a four point six percent drop in twenty twenty-three. It quotes carrying costs of twenty-five to thirty-five thousand in one place and twenty-four to forty-eight in another. Because of such inconsistencies, we treat the page as a rough guide, not a data source.
scenes.caption: AUTOMONITOR INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES (OUR READING OF THE PAGE): 'CONSISTENTLY GAINED VALUE' vs 2023 −4.6% · CARRYING COSTS $25–35K vs $24–48K · PRODUCTION 1,826 vs 1,763

scenes.text: Depreciation is the hardest to pin down. Lambocars, citing CarEdge, says an Aventador loses up to thirty-one percent of its value over five years at twelve thousand miles a year, and a Huracán forty-six percent. A three hundred twenty thousand dollar Aventador would lose almost one hundred thousand dollars, by the article's math and ours.
scenes.caption: LAMBOCARS (CITING CAREDGE): AVENTADOR UP TO −31% / 5 YR AT 12,000 MI/YR; HURACÁN −46% · $320,000 × 31% = $99,200 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, that is about twenty thousand dollars a year, or fifty-four hundred dollars a month, which is more than the newsletter's low estimate for service and insurance combined. But the SVJ is a different story if the unsourced Automonitor table is right: it shows the coupé's average value rising from five hundred thirty to six hundred sixty thousand between twenty twenty and an estimated twenty twenty-five.
scenes.caption: $99,200 ÷ 5 = $19,840/YR; ÷ 12 = $1,653/MONTH (OUR ARITHMETIC) · AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED) SVJ COUPÉ AVERAGE VALUE: 2020 $530K → 2025 EST. $660K (+24.5%, OUR ARITHMETIC) · SOURCE NAMED: BRING A TRAILER; NO DATA SHOWN

scenes.text: The limited-edition cars behave differently. Wikipedia says the last Ultimae coupé sold for over one point six million dollars at RM Sotheby's in April twenty twenty-two, with a digital token. The delivery table shows that the Aventador sold seven hundred ninety-eight cars in twenty twenty-one and seven hundred fifty-three in twenty twenty-two. A rare last-of-line car is a different asset from a common one.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: LAST ULTIMAE COUPÉ > $1.6 M, RM SOTHEBY'S, APRIL 2022, WITH A 1-OF-1 NFT · DELIVERIES 798 (2021), 753 (2022) · 'DIFFERENT ASSET' = OUR READING

scenes.text: Production volume matters for value. Wikipedia says total Aventador production was eleven thousand eight hundred thirty-one, against a plan of four thousand. By our arithmetic, that is almost three times the plan. A model built in large numbers tends to hold less of a scarcity premium than a limited one, though our sources do not state a rule.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 11,831 BUILT vs 4,000 PLANNED · 11,831 ÷ 4,000 = 2.96× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 'LESS SCARCITY PREMIUM' = OUR INFERENCE; NO RULE STATED IN SOURCES

scenes.text: Scale. The Census Bureau puts median U.S. household income for twenty twenty-four at eighty-three thousand seven hundred thirty dollars. By our arithmetic, the newsletter's yearly ownership cost of thirty-four thousand three hundred to forty-six thousand three hundred is forty-one to fifty-five percent of that income, before the car is bought.
scenes.caption: CENSUS 2024 MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME $83,730 · $34,300 ÷ $83,730 = 41.0%; $46,300 ÷ $83,730 = 55.3% (OUR ARITHMETIC; GROSS INCOME)
scenes.chapter: Scale: what it means for a household

scenes.text: Kelley Blue Book put the average new vehicle at fifty thousand and eighty-nine dollars in August twenty twenty-six. By our arithmetic, the three hundred seven thousand dollar purchase is six point one average new vehicles, and the SVJ's base price of five hundred seventeen thousand seven hundred seventy is ten point three. A year of running the Aventador costs up to nine tenths of one average car.
scenes.caption: KBB: AVG NEW VEHICLE AUG 2026 $50,089 · $307,000 ÷ $50,089 = 6.1 · $517,770 ÷ $50,089 = 10.3 · $46,300 ÷ $50,089 = 0.92 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Putting it together for a five-year scenario, using only the newsletter's figures and the Lambocars depreciation. Purchase three hundred seven thousand dollars. Five years of running costs at thirty-four thousand three hundred to forty-six thousand three hundred, which is one hundred seventy-one thousand five hundred to two hundred thirty-one thousand five hundred. Depreciation of up to thirty-one percent, about ninety-five thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: $307,000 PURCHASE · 5 × $34,300 = $171,500; 5 × $46,300 = $231,500 · $307,000 × 31% = $95,170 (OUR ARITHMETIC; NEWSLETTER + LAMBOCARS FIGURES; ESTIMATES MIXED)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, running costs plus depreciation come to two hundred sixty-six thousand six hundred seventy to three hundred twenty-six thousand six hundred seventy, which is eighty-seven to one hundred six percent of the purchase price over five years. In other words, on these estimates the cost of five years of ownership matches the price of the car. They are estimates, mixed from different years and sources.
scenes.caption: $171,500 + $95,170 = $266,670; $231,500 + $95,170 = $326,670 · ÷ $307,000 = 86.9%–106.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC; MIXED ESTIMATES FROM DIFFERENT YEARS AND SOURCES)

scenes.text: Let us turn the yearly bill into a cost per mile, using the newsletter's own assumption of five thousand miles a year. By our arithmetic, thirty-four thousand three hundred divided by five thousand is six dollars eighty-six a mile, and forty-six thousand three hundred divided by five thousand is nine dollars twenty-six. That excludes depreciation, finance charges and the purchase price.
scenes.caption: $34,300 ÷ 5,000 = $6.86/MI · $46,300 ÷ 5,000 = $9.26/MI (OUR ARITHMETIC; NEWSLETTER'S 5,000 MI/YR ASSUMPTION; EXCLUDES DEPRECIATION AND FINANCING)

scenes.text: Add the Lambocars depreciation of about twenty thousand dollars a year, from thirty-one percent of three hundred twenty thousand over five years. By our arithmetic, that raises the total to about fifty-four thousand to sixty-six thousand dollars a year, or eleven to thirteen dollars a mile at five thousand miles. Those are mixed estimates, so we round them.
scenes.caption: $34,300 + $19,840 = $54,140; $46,300 + $19,840 = $66,140 · ÷ 5,000 = $10.83–$13.23/MI (OUR ARITHMETIC; MIXES TWO SOURCES AND A $320,000 CAR WITH A $307,000 CAR)

scenes.text: Driving more reduces the fixed part of the cost. The Lambocars depreciation estimate assumes twelve thousand miles a year. By our arithmetic, at twelve thousand miles, the newsletter's non-fuel costs of thirty-one thousand five hundred to forty-three thousand five hundred come to two dollars sixty-two to three dollars sixty-two a mile, before fuel and mileage-related depreciation.
scenes.caption: NEWSLETTER NON-FUEL COSTS: $34,300 − $2,812 = $31,488; $46,300 − $2,812 = $43,488 · ÷ 12,000 = $2.62–$3.62/MI (OUR ARITHMETIC; ASSUMES COSTS DO NOT RISE WITH MILES — OUR SIMPLIFICATION)

scenes.text: Fuel at twelve thousand miles and Autocar's eleven point nine miles per gallon is about one thousand eight gallons, by our arithmetic, or four thousand three hundred twenty dollars at the regular price of four dollars twenty-eight. Lambocars' upper figure of sixty-six hundred dollars is consistent with a higher premium price or more miles. Our sources give no premium price to check it.
scenes.caption: 12,000 ÷ 11.9 = 1,008 GAL × $4.284 = $4,320 (OUR ARITHMETIC; REGULAR PRICE) · LAMBOCARS UP TO $6,600 · PREMIUM PRICE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Automonitor lists unexpected repairs over five years at five thousand to thirty-five thousand dollars, with individual items: an E-gear actuator at eight to fifteen thousand, a clutch at twelve to eighteen thousand, lift motors at three to five thousand each, and rear wing service at two to four thousand every four to six years. Unsourced, and its own conservative total is lower than a single actuator job.
scenes.caption: AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): UNEXPECTED REPAIRS (5 YR) $5–35K · E-GEAR ACTUATOR $8–15K · CLUTCH $12–18K · LIFT MOTOR $3–5K EACH · REAR WING SERVICE $2–4K EVERY 4–6 YR · CONSERVATIVE $5K < ONE ACTUATOR JOB $8K (OUR OBSERVATION)

scenes.text: Protection costs: paint protection film at six to ten thousand dollars and ceramic coating at fifteen hundred to three thousand, from the same page. By our arithmetic, film plus coating at the low end is seventy-five hundred dollars, and at the high end thirteen thousand. Neither is mentioned by the newsletter or by Lambocars, so we cannot cross-check them.
scenes.caption: AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): PPF $6–10K; CERAMIC COATING $1.5–3K · $6,000 + $1,500 = $7,500; $10,000 + $3,000 = $13,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · CROSS-CHECK: NONE IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Registration and property tax appear as a range on the Automonitor page: over five thousand dollars a year in California, some states five hundred or less, and property tax of three to seven thousand where applicable. The newsletter assumes fifteen hundred a year for registration and taxes. By our arithmetic, California's alone would be more than three times that.
scenes.caption: AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): REGISTRATION / PROPERTY TAX CALIFORNIA > $5K/YR; SOME STATES ≤ $500; PROPERTY TAX $3–7K WHERE APPLICABLE · NEWSLETTER: $1,500/YR · $5,000 ÷ $1,500 = 3.3× (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Options matter on a new car. Autocar lists heated electric seats at three thousand pounds and the Sensonum sound system at three thousand one hundred fifty-six. By our arithmetic, those two together are sixty-one hundred fifty-six pounds, about one and a half percent of a four-hundred-thousand-pound test car. The test car cost well over four hundred thousand, the review says.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR: HEATED SEATS £3,000 · SENSONUM £3,156 · £6,156 ÷ £400,000 = 1.5% (OUR ARITHMETIC; TEST CAR 'WELL OVER £400,000')

scenes.text: The Autocar review also gives cabin noise of ninety-six decibels at eighty-five hundred revs in third gear. It calls the seven-inch screen outdated, and criticises the gearbox. Those are costs of a different kind: comfort and usability. By our arithmetic, a car that is loud at its engine's best revs is one you pay for in more than money, but that is our reading of the review.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR: 96 DB AT 8,500 RPM IN 3RD; 7-IN SCREEN 'OUTDATED'; GEARBOX CRITICISED · 'PAY IN MORE THAN MONEY' = OUR READING

scenes.text: Automonitor's five-year table for a six hundred fifty thousand dollar car gives three scenarios. Conservative: a carrying cost of one hundred twenty thousand dollars, with eighty thousand of appreciation, for a net forty thousand. Moderate: one hundred sixty-six thousand five hundred, sixty thousand of appreciation, net one hundred six thousand five hundred. High use: two hundred forty thousand, thirty thousand, net two hundred ten thousand.
scenes.caption: AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): 5-YR TCO ON A $650K CAR — CONSERVATIVE $120K COST, +$80K APPRECIATION, NET $40K · MODERATE $166.5K, +$60K, NET $106.5K · HIGH USE $240K, +$30K, NET $210K · ARITHMETIC CONSISTENT (OUR CHECK)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, those net costs are six, sixteen and thirty-two percent of the car's price over five years. The numbers depend entirely on appreciation, which the page assumes and our other sources neither confirm nor deny for the SVJ. Lambocars, by contrast, cites an average Aventador depreciation of up to thirty-one percent. The two views are opposites.
scenes.caption: $40K ÷ $650K = 6.2% · $106.5K ÷ $650K = 16.4% · $210K ÷ $650K = 32.3% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · AUTOMONITOR ASSUMES APPRECIATION; LAMBOCARS CITES DEPRECIATION OF UP TO 31% FOR THE AVENTADOR GENERALLY

scenes.text: They can both be right: a general Aventador can lose value while a limited SVJ gains it. Our sources do not settle it. Wikipedia says the SVJ was limited to nine hundred coupés, though that number needs a citation, and lists six hundred each for the Ultimae and the SV. The scarcer the car, the more the appreciation story can hold.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: SVJ 900 COUPÉS ([CITATION NEEDED]) · ULTIMAE 600 · SV 600 COUPÉS + 500 ROADSTERS · 'SCARCER, MORE APPRECIATION' = OUR INFERENCE; SOURCES DO NOT SETTLE IT

scenes.text: The wide spread in used prices supports that. Three hundred fifteen thousand dollars for a twenty sixteen car and nine hundred seventy-five thousand for a twenty twenty SVJ Roadster. By our arithmetic, the SVJ Roadster listing is seventy percent above its original base price of five hundred seventy-three thousand nine hundred sixty-six. A listing is an ask, not a sale, so the real price may be lower.
scenes.caption: LAMBOCARS: 2020 SVJ ROADSTER LISTED $975,000 · AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): ROADSTER MSRP $573,966 · $975,000 ÷ $573,966 = 1.70× (+70%) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · LISTING = ASK, NOT SALE PRICE

scenes.text: Lambocars compares prices across the range: a base Huracán at about two hundred thousand dollars, the Huracán STO at three hundred thirty thousand, the Urus at two hundred twenty-five thousand, and used Aventadors from three hundred fifteen thousand. By our arithmetic, the cheapest used Aventador listing costs about fifty-eight percent more than a new base Huracán.
scenes.caption: LAMBOCARS (4 MAY 2022): HURACÁN BASE ~$200,000 · STO $330,000 · URUS $225,000 · USED AVENTADOR FROM $315,000 (2016) · $315,000 ÷ $200,000 = 1.58× (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT AGES AND DATES)
scenes.chapter: If you chose a cheaper Lamborghini

scenes.text: On depreciation, Lambocars says a Huracán loses forty-six percent over five years, against up to thirty-one for an Aventador. By our arithmetic, a two-hundred-thousand-dollar Huracán would lose ninety-two thousand dollars, about the same as the almost one hundred thousand lost by a three-hundred-twenty-thousand-dollar Aventador. The cheaper car loses nearly as much in dollars.
scenes.caption: LAMBOCARS (CITING CAREDGE): HURACÁN −46%; AVENTADOR UP TO −31% · $200,000 × 46% = $92,000 vs $320,000 × 31% = $99,200 (OUR ARITHMETIC; MODEL AVERAGES, NOT STO / SVJ)

scenes.text: Wikipedia gives fuel figures for the base Aventador of seventeen point two litres per hundred kilometres, which by our arithmetic is thirteen point seven miles per gallon, and a carbon dioxide output of 398 grams per kilometre. Autocar measured the SVJ at eleven point nine miles per gallon and 452 grams. By our arithmetic, the SVJ burns about fifteen percent more fuel per mile than the base car's official figure.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (LP 700-4): 17.2 L/100 KM (13.7 US MPG, OUR CONVERSION); 398 G/KM · AUTOCAR (SVJ): 11.9 MPG; 452 G/KM · 13.7 ÷ 11.9 = +15.1% FUEL PER MILE (OUR ARITHMETIC; OFFICIAL vs MEASURED — NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE)

scenes.text: For a lesser extreme, the Lambocars article describes a track-day insurance package of about three thousand dollars a weekend, which does not cover consumables like brake pads and tyres. It does not price those consumables. The Automonitor page prices carbon-ceramic pads alone at three to five thousand dollars every fifteen to twenty thousand miles, again unsourced.
scenes.caption: LAMBOCARS: TRACK-DAY INSURANCE PACKAGE ~$3,000/WEEKEND; PADS AND TYRES NOT COVERED, NOT PRICED · AUTOMONITOR (UNSOURCED): PADS $3–5K EVERY 15–20K MILES; ROTOR LIFE 40–60K MI STREET, 15–25K TRACK

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, one track weekend of three thousand dollars is almost nine percent of the newsletter's low yearly estimate of thirty-four thousand three hundred. It covers nothing but insurance. The consumables are the unknown, and our sources do not give them for the SVJ, so a track-day owner's real bill is higher than any figure here.
scenes.caption: $3,000 ÷ $34,300 = 8.7% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · CONSUMABLES FOR THE SVJ: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: One more frame: the Autocar road test says the SVJ is a car with a roofline sixty millimetres lower than a McLaren seven twenty S, and a twenty-twenty-five republication date. Why does that matter for ownership? It may not, but it points to how specialised the car is. We have no source on how this affects insurance, parking or access, so we leave it there.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR (PAGE DATED 30 JUN 2025): ROOFLINE 60 MM LOWER THAN A McLAREN 720S · EFFECT ON INSURANCE / PARKING: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: To recap the pieces, with their sources. The car: three hundred seven thousand dollars for a twenty thirteen example. The yearly bill: thirty-four to forty-six thousand, from the newsletter. Fuel: anywhere from eighteen hundred to sixty-six hundred, depending on miles and price. Depreciation: up to thirty-one percent over five years, from Lambocars. Everything else, from Automonitor, is flagged as unsourced.
scenes.caption: RECAP: PURCHASE $307,000 (GARAGE INTELLIGENCE) · YEARLY $34.3–46.3K (GARAGE INTELLIGENCE) · FUEL $1,800 (OUR FLOOR) TO $6,600 (LAMBOCARS) · DEPRECIATION UP TO 31% / 5 YR (LAMBOCARS, CITING CAREDGE) · AUTOMONITOR = UNSOURCED

scenes.text: What is missing. Any figure from a documented owner for an SVJ. An official service schedule or price list from Lamborghini. Premium fuel prices. A source for the Automonitor numbers. Insurance quotes from a named insurer. The SVJ's real depreciation, as opposed to the Aventador average. If you have a primary document for any of these, put it in the comments.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: DOCUMENTED SVJ OWNER COSTS · OFFICIAL SERVICE SCHEDULE / PRICES · PREMIUM FUEL PRICE · SOURCES FOR AUTOMONITOR · NAMED-INSURER QUOTES · SVJ-SPECIFIC DEPRECIATION
scenes.chapter: What the sources do not say

scenes.text: So the real cost of owning an Aventador is not the sticker. It is the sticker, plus a yearly bill that one source puts at thirty-four to forty-six thousand dollars, plus whatever the car loses or gains in value. In the other videos this week we reveal the SVJ's two lesser-known facts, compare it with the Huracán STO, and tell why the Aventador was the last of its kind. Subscribe to Pickup Reality.
